name: Soil Testing & Conservation

objectives.text: Identify signs of healthy soil such as dark color, crumbly structure, plant roots, and earthworms
Describe how wind and running water carry soil away from bare ground
Explain why farmers and gardeners test soil before planting a crop
Explain why protecting soil from loss is part of responsible stewardship of farmland
Demonstrate with a simple runoff model how plant cover reduces soil erosion compared with bare soil
Demonstrate proper technique for collecting a representative composite soil sample from a field or garden, including sampling pattern, depth, and labeling
Measure soil pH with a test kit or meter and record the results in a data table
Identify the types of soil erosion including sheet, rill, gully, and wind erosion from field observations or photographs
Interpret a soil test report to identify pH, organic matter, and nutrient levels that fall below, within, or above optimum ranges
Describe common soil conservation practices such as no-till, contour farming, strip cropping, terracing, windbreaks, and grassed waterways
Identify soil sampling tools and techniques such as soil probes, augers, and core samplers used to collect samples for laboratory and field analysis
Analyze the chemistry of a soil sample using laboratory tests for pH, nitrate, phosphorus, and potassium
Summarize how sustainable production methods such as crop rotation, companion planting, and cover crops build and protect soil
Compare soil health measurements such as organic matter, soil respiration, infiltration, and aggregate stability to determine their effectiveness and limitations
Analyze the causes of soil erosion on a site and evaluate the effectiveness of competing erosion control practices
Determine the land capability class of a site from slope, soil depth, erosion, and soil survey data as practiced in the FFA Land Evaluation CDE
Estimate annual soil loss for a field using the factors of the Universal Soil Loss Equation
Evaluate a soil sample to determine its overall quality and whether it has been contaminated
Analyze a plot of land to determine which soil management and conservation techniques are most applicable
Evaluate how NRCS conservation programs such as EQIP and CRP could support conservation practices on a farm operation
Design a soil conservation and stewardship plan for a selected cropping system that integrates soil test data and erosion control practices to build topsoil and productivity
Design and conduct an SAE research project that measures the effect of a conservation practice on soil health indicators and present the findings

changes: Kept all six original competencies, rewording several for precision (healthy soil signs, sampling technique with composite pattern and depth, reading a soil test report limited to interpretation so fertilizer prescription stays with Soil Fertility & Fertilizers). Split the grade 10 erosion objective into erosion types, conservation practice description, and causal analysis with evaluation. Added early stewardship and runoff model objectives, pH measurement, sampling tools, laboratory soil chemistry, sustainable production methods, soil health indicator comparison, land capability classification tied to the FFA Land Evaluation CDE, USLE soil loss estimation, contamination evaluation, site analysis, NRCS program evaluation, and an SAE research capstone. Excluded soil formation, texture and soil water, pH and CEC of media, and fertilizer prescription as sibling material. Standards assigned only at grades 9 to 12 where the objective directly teaches the standard.
